title: Logout leaves the bearer token persisted

evidence.quote: setToken persists ghostwriter_token in localStorage, and getToken reloads it from localStorage.
async logout(): Promise<void> { await this.request('/auth/logout', { method: 'POST' }); }

reasoning: The client stores the bearer token with setToken(), but logout() only POSTs to the logout endpoint and never clears the in-memory or localStorage token. After a successful logout call, getToken() and isAuthenticated() can still report the old token, and future API calls will continue sending it.
reproduction: Mock fetch to return 200 for /auth/logout, call api.setToken('token'), then await api.logout(); api.getToken() still returns 'token'.
recommendation: Clear the client token as part of logout, preferably in a finally block so an explicit user logout discards local credentials even if the network request fails.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for the frontend API client token lifecycle.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a frontend API client test that sets a token, mocks a successful logout response, calls logout(), and asserts localStorage no longer contains ghostwriter_token and getToken() returns null.
minimumFixScope: Update ApiClient.logout() in frontend/src/lib/api/client.ts to call setToken(null) after attempting the logout request.
